With 480 trainable parameters on 1500 items and 700 full-batch Adam steps, arm ranking on unseen data is unknown; mismatched-order chains (fitting a non-realizable function) could over-fit more than the matching chain, so the true held-out order gap could be larger OR smaller. The conclusion cannot be read as stated until re-run with a distinct test draw (different seed or n for the test call).

findings.title: The status word CAS_PRECEDENCE_VALUE_NOT_ESTABLISHED in the commit message was NOT emitted by the program; the program's own branch says 'do NOT substitute a new hypothesis'
findings.evidence: Line 232: `pred_a, pred_b, pred_c = d_a > 0.02, abs(d_b) < 0.03, d_c < -0.02`. With the commit's numbers d_a=+0.0219 (True), d_b=-0.0061 (True), d_c=-0.0136 (False). Line 240: `if pred_a and pred_b and pred_c:` guards line 246 `STATUS: CAS_PRECEDENCE_VALUE_NOT_ESTABLISHED`; this branch did not fire. Line 248 `elif pred_b and not pred_a:` did not fire (pred_a True). Lines 251-253 (the branch that fired): `else:` / `THE PREDICTION DID NOT HOLD AS REGISTERED. Report exactly which part failed` / `and do NOT substitute a new hypothesis for the registered one.` Commit 1e58d725 message: `(c) ... (predicted < -0.02, FAILED)` then `=> order matters, CAS ordering does not. CAS_PRECEDENCE_VALUE_NOT_ESTABLISHED.` The status word appears at HEAD only inside the script's un-fired print (line 246) and in the commit message; no results file exists (git ls-files under CJT_PREC_CLOSURE lists only .py/.md; none of CLOSURE_FINDINGS.md, THEOREM_AUDIT_PACKAGE.md, docs/CAS_HARNESS_SPEC_SHEET.md, CHANGELOG.md contain the order-test numbers or the status word).
findings.effect_on_conclusion: The reported status is prose reinterpretation after a failed registered prediction, which the script's own text and the owner's rule ('claim status must come from a deterministic program reading') forbid. The only program-emitted verdict is 'THE PREDICTION DID NOT HOLD AS REGISTERED' on part (c). The direction the commit asserts (winner set by the world) may still be right, but it is not what this program produced.

findings.title: POSITIVE control is a capacity/interaction test, not an order-matching test: chain arms have 480 trainable parameters with recurrent cross-type interaction, the bag has 224 and is purely additive
findings.evidence: Lines 91-95 `init`: W = K*(DE*H) = 4*40 = 160; U = K*(H*H) = 4*64 = 256 (`np.zeros((H, H)) if bag else rng.normal(...)`); b = K*H = 32; R = H*NCLS = 32. Chain total 480; bag trainable 224 (U frozen: line 129 `g["U"][j] = np.zeros((H, H))`, verified U stays exactly zero under the Adam update at lines 141-143). Line 101 bag forward: `h = sum(np.tanh(E[:, order[j], :] @ p["W"][j] + p["b"][j]) for j in range(K))` -- a sum over types, no term couples two types. Line 105 chain forward: `h = np.tanh(E[:, order[j], :] @ p["W"][j] + h @ p["U"][j].T + p["b"][j])` -- multiplicative interaction via U. The world (line 60) `s = np.tanh(E[:, t, :] @ A[j] + s @ B[j].T)` has the chain's exact functional form, so the matching chain is realizable and the bag is not. Line 204: `pos_ok = (A[cas][0] > A[bag][0] + 0.02) and (Cc[rev][0] > Cc[bag][0] + 0.02)` compares matching CHAIN vs BAG only. Commit: 'BAG mechanism-free loses by 0.13-0.15 everywhere ordered' while the MISMATCHED chains sit within 0.0219 / 0.0136 of the matching chain, i.e. a wrong-order chain still beats the bag by roughly 0.11-0.13.
findings.effect_on_conclusion: 'Order matters' in the commit is almost entirely 'a recurrent chain beats an additive bag' -- an asymmetry in parameter count (480 vs 224) and representational class, present with any order. The order-specific effect is only the +0.0219 / -0.0136 match-vs-mismatch gap. The positive control therefore does not certify that the harness can detect order-matching at the 0.02 scale it then uses as the verdict threshold.

findings.title: Conditions (a) and (c) are mirror images measuring the same quantity twice; the 0.02 threshold falls between the two realisations, so 'HELD' vs 'FAILED' is a threshold artifact
findings.evidence: Lines 181-182: `make_world(r, CAS_ORDER, n)` and `make_world(r, REVERSED, n)` with the same seeds 1000+sd (line 160). make_world (lines 51-54) draws A, B, C, E from the rng before the order is used, so (a) and (c) share identical A, B, C, E; only the composition order at line 60 differs (verified: `E identical=True`, label agreement 0.2113-0.3300 per seed). E's K type channels are i.i.d. (line 54 `E = rng.normal(0, 1, (n, K, DE))`), so relabelling types maps world-CAS/arm-CAS onto world-REV/arm-REV exactly in distribution. Both non-matching arms are full derangements in both worlds: verified `positions matched = 0/4` for REV and RANDFIX vs world CAS and for CAS and RANDFIX vs world REV. Lines 224-225: `d_a = A[cas][0] - max(A[rev][0], A[ran][0])` (>= +0.0219) and `d_c = Cc[cas][0] - Cc[rev][0]` (-0.0136). Line 232 thresholds `d_a > 0.02` and `d_c < -0.02`.
findings.effect_on_conclusion: Match-minus-mismatch was realised as >= 0.0219 in (a) and 0.0136 in (c); the registered 0.02 line sits between two draws of the same effect. That the sign pattern flips with the world's order actually supports 'the world sets the winner', but the HELD/FAILED labels the program printed reflect noise around a fixed constant, not a difference between the CAS order and the reversed order. The registered prediction (c) 'FAILED' is not evidence that CAS resists losing.

findings.title: 5 seeds, absolute thresholds not calibrated to noise, per-arm sd instead of paired-difference sd; +0.0219 vs threshold 0.02 is a 0.0019 margin that the commit itself labels '~1 seed sd'
findings.evidence: Line 41 `SEEDS = 5`. Line 167: `return {k: (float(np.mean(v)), float(np.std(v, ddof=1))) for k, v in acc.items()}` -- the sd is across the 5 seed-level accuracies (seed sd, not item sd), and the per-seed vectors are discarded here. Lines 159-166: every arm shares the same world (Etr/ytr) per seed and the same init seed `np.random.default_rng(7000 + sd)` (verified: the three chain arms have identical initial W, U, b, R), so the design is PAIRED, but lines 224-226 compare unpaired means of means and line 230 prints `seed sd approx {max(Bb[k][1] for k in (cas, rev, ran)):.4f}` = the largest single-arm sd in (b), not the sd of the CAS-minus-other difference. Thresholds are fixed constants: line 204 `+ 0.02`, line 206 `< 0.05`, line 232 `> 0.02`, `< 0.03`, `< -0.02`. Commit: '(a) ... +0.0219 (~1 seed sd)' and '(b) ... seed sd 0.0301'. With per-arm seed sd 0.0301, SE of a 5-seed mean is 0.0301/sqrt(5) = 0.0135 and an unpaired difference SE is about 0.019 -- the same size as the 0.02 threshold. The paired-difference sd, which could be smaller, is never computed or printed; the (a) and (c) sds exist only in un-captured stdout.
findings.effect_on_conclusion: Neither +0.0219 (a) nor -0.0136 (c) nor -0.0061 (b) can be distinguished from seed noise from what is reported. The HELD/FAILED labels are readings of a fixed constant against a noisy mean with n=5 and no test statistic. The only differences clearly above noise are chain-vs-bag (0.13-0.15), which is the capacity asymmetry, not order.

findings.title: Prediction (b) 'all fixed orders tie' holds by symmetry of the world, so it cannot inform about CAS
findings.evidence: Lines 72-77: `order = rng.permutation(K)` redrawn per item, then `s = np.tanh(E[i, order[j], :] @ A[j] + B[j] @ s)`. Because the true order is a uniform random permutation per item and E's type channels are i.i.d., any fixed arm order is equally mismatched in distribution; the three fixed-order arms are exchangeable. Line 23: `The prediction is FALSIFIED if the CAS arm wins in (b)` -- a clause that can only trip by noise. Line 226 `d_b = Bb[cas][0] - max(Bb[rev][0], Bb[ran][0])` additionally biases d_b negative (max of two noisy arms).
findings.effect_on_conclusion: The 'DEAD TIE' in (b) is guaranteed by construction and carries no information about the CAS order; it functions only as a noise-level readout (0.0301). It should not be counted as a held falsifiable prediction.

findings.title: 'Registered before running' is not verifiable from git; script and its numbers first appear in the same commit, and no output artifact exists at HEAD
findings.evidence: `git log --format='%H %ad %s' --date=short -- cas_only_reasoner/CJT_PREC_CLOSURE/p6_order_test.py` returns a single entry: `1e58d7254d97c88effa609f7ad05ee2fca9b1aee 2026-09-02 P6 order test + visibility law + DeepSeek R1 independent audit PASS`. That commit's message already carries 0.9689 / 0.9471 / +0.0219 / 0.9312 / 0.9448 / -0.0136 / 0.7245 / 0.7307 / -0.0061 / 0.0301. Lines 15-17 and 174 claim the prediction was 'written BEFORE any number is produced', but there is no earlier commit of the file and the script writes no results file (no file open / json dump anywhere in lines 1-253). `git grep` at HEAD for the numbers finds none of them in any CJT_PREC_CLOSURE file, the spec sheet, or CHANGELOG.md (the four spec-sheet 'P6' hits at lines 1376, 1377, 1406, 1407 are the unrelated CMB-P0 arm).

Direction of the conclusion unaffected, but the audit trail the docstring promises does not exist at HEAD.

findings.title: Only 3 of the 24 fixed orders were tested; RANDOM_FIXED 'chosen once, never tuned' is unverifiable
findings.evidence: Lines 42-44: `CAS_ORDER = (0, 1, 2, 3)`, `REVERSED = (3, 2, 1, 0)`, `RANDOM_FIXED = (2, 0, 3, 1)       # one fixed non-CAS order, chosen once, never tuned`. Lines 151-154 define exactly four arms: three fixed orders plus the bag. No sweep over the remaining 21 permutations, and no partially-matching order (both non-CAS orders are 0/4 derangements against both world orders).
findings.effect_on_conclusion: The claim 'best other fixed order' means best of two, both full derangements. Nothing is known about orders sharing 1-3 positions with the world, which is where an intrinsic-order claim would be graded. Does not change direction.

findings.title: Bag arm's readout R is initialised from a different random draw than the chain arms' R
findings.evidence: Line 93: `U=[np.zeros((H, H)) if bag else rng.normal(0, .4, (H, H)) for _ in range(K)]` -- in the bag case rng.normal is never called for U, so the subsequent draw at line 95 `R=rng.normal(0, .4, (H, NCLS))` comes from an earlier point in the stream. Verified: bag W identical to chain W = True, bag R identical to chain R = False. Chain arms are identical to each other at init (verified True).
findings.effect_on_conclusion: Not load-bearing (a 32-value readout init), but the chain-vs-bag comparison is not perfectly paired on init while the chain-vs-chain comparisons are. Direction unaffected.

findings.title: Negative control excludes the bag arm and includes only the three chain arms; the comparator in (a) uses max of two arms
findings.evidence: Line 205: `spread_neg = max(Ng[k][0] for k in (cas, rev, ran)) - min(Ng[k][0] for k in (cas, rev, ran))` -- bag omitted. Line 224: `d_a = A[cas][0] - max(A[rev][0], A[ran][0])` -- max-of-two comparator makes d_a conservative for CAS but is not symmetric with line 225 `d_c = Cc[cas][0] - Cc[rev][0]` (single comparator).
findings.effect_on_conclusion: (a) and (c) use different comparators for what is by symmetry the same quantity, which contributes to the (a)-HELD / (c)-FAILED split. Small effect; direction unaffected.

p6_lenses.world_generation_answer_key: The label is a deterministic function of the evidence E with no noise. Lines 48-62 `make_world`: per condition, A (K matrices DE x H), B (K matrices H x H), C (H x NCLS) and E (n x K x DE, i.i.d. normal type channels) are drawn from the seed BEFORE the order is used; then line 60 `s = np.tanh(E[:, t, :] @ A[j] + s @ B[j].T)` composes types in `true_order` and line 61 `y = np.argmax(s @ C, axis=1)`. The chain arm's forward (line 105) has exactly this functional form (W<->A, U<->B, R<->C, b=0), so the arm whose order equals the world's order is the generator itself (realizable); any other fixed order is a mismatch of equal capacity; the bag (line 101) cannot represent the cross-type interaction at all. The true order is swept as a condition (lines 180-185): (a) CAS (0,1,2,3), (c) REVERSED (3,2,1,0), (b) per-item random permutation (lines 72-77, no fixed order can match), NEG no-structure bag world (line 86). Consequences verified outside the repo: (a) and (c) share identical A, B, C, E for each seed (only composition order differs; label agreement 0.2113-0.3300); REVERSED and RANDOM_FIXED (2,0,3,1) both match 0/4 positions of both world orders, so both 'other' arms are full derangements; (b) makes all fixed orders exchangeable, so its tie is by construction. The world's true order is therefore the answer key: the arm that carries it wins by realizability, whichever order it is -- which is exactly what the script set out to show, but the design makes (a) and (c) two draws of one quantity rather than two independent tests.
p6_lenses.registered_before_run_verifiable: NO. The file has a single commit in its history: 1e58d7254d97c88effa609f7ad05ee2fca9b1aee (2026-09-02, 'P6 order test + visibility law + DeepSeek R1 independent audit PASS'), and that same commit's message already reports every result number (0.9689, 0.9471, +0.0219, 0.9312, 0.9448, -0.0136, 0.7245, 0.7307, -0.0061, 0.0301, 'bag loses by 0.13-0.15'). The docstring (lines 15-17) and banner (line 174 'written before running') assert pre-registration, but there is no earlier commit of the prediction, no results/output file is written by the script (lines 1-253 contain no file write), and no result file is tracked at HEAD (`git ls-files -- cas_only_reasoner/CJT_PREC_CLOSURE` lists only .py and .md files, none of which contain the order-test numbers). Where the numbers live: ONLY in the commit message of 1e58d725. Not in any artifact file at HEAD; not in docs/CAS_HARNESS_SPEC_SHEET.md (its 'P6' hits at lines 1376, 1377, 1406, 1407 are the unrelated CMB-P0 arm); not in CHANGELOG.md; not in CLOSURE_FINDINGS.md or THEOREM_AUDIT_PACKAGE.md (their 1e58d725 diffs concern the visibility law and the defect-#20 table correction only).
p6_lenses.held_out_is_held_out: NOT HELD OUT -- the test set IS the training set. Line 40: `NTR, NTE, STEPS, LR = 1500, 1500, 700, 0.05`. Line 160: `rng = np.random.default_rng(1000 + sd)`; line 161: `Etr, ytr = worldfn(rng, NTR)`; line 162: `Ete, yte = worldfn(np.random.default_rng(1000 + sd), NTE)  # same world, fresh draw`; line 163: `Ete, yte = Ete[:NTE], yte[:NTE]`. The test call re-seeds with the identical seed 1000+sd and the identical n=1500, so every world function draws the same A, B, C, permutations and E; line 163 slices 1500 to 1500 (no-op). Verified by exec-ing only the definitions portion of the script (no training) in a throwaway numpy check: for conditions (a), (c), (b) and NEG and for all seeds 0-4, `E identical=True  y identical=True  n_tr=1500 n_te=1500`. Line 147-148 evaluate accuracy on Ete/yte, i.e. on the training items. Line 173 prints '1500 train / 1500 held out', which is false. Every accuracy in the commit message (0.9689, 0.9471, 0.9312, 0.9448, 0.7245, 0.7307, the bag gaps 0.13-0.15) is a training-set accuracy.
p6_lenses.arms_matched: Parameters (lines 91-95, K=4, DE=5, H=8, NCLS=4): chain arms (P5 CAS, P6a reversed, P6b random fixed) W 4x(5x8)=160, U 4x(8x8)=256, b 4x8=32, R 8x4=32 = 480 trainable. BAG arm: W 160, b 32, R 32 = 224 trainable; U is 256 zeros (line 93), receives zero gradient (line 129) and verified to stay exactly zero under the Adam update (lines 141-143) -- so the bag has 224 trainable vs 480, and no cross-type interaction term at all (line 101 additive sum vs line 105 recurrent `h @ p[\"U\"][j].T`). Compute per step: chain forward ~ K*n*DE*H + K*n*H*H + n*H*NCLS = 240000 + 384000 + 48000 = 672000 multiply-adds; bag forward 288000 plus a recomputed tanh in its backward (line 125) -- chain is roughly 2.3x the bag's compute per step. Steps: 700 for every arm (line 40, line 116). Optimiser: full-batch Adam, beta1 .9, beta2 .999, eps 1e-8, bias-corrected (lines 141-146), LR 0.05 for every arm (line 143, 146). Init: all three chain arms identical at init (seed 7000+sd, verified); bag shares the chain's W and b but its R is a different draw (line 93 skips the U draws). Worlds paired across arms per seed (lines 159-166). Asymmetry that explains 'order matters' without order: the chain-vs-bag gap (0.13-0.15) is a capacity/representation gap -- 480 vs 224 parameters and recurrent interaction vs additive -- and mismatched-order chains also beat the bag by roughly 0.11-0.13; the order-specific gap is only +0.0219 / -0.0136. Hyperparameters were not tuned per arm (single setting), so chain-vs-chain comparisons are fair; the positive control (line 204) is not.
p6_lenses.verdict_on_specific_cas_order_value: NOT ESTABLISHED IN EITHER DIRECTION BY THIS SCRIPT AS COMMITTED. What survives: the sign pattern (the CAS-ordered arm is best when the world is CAS-ordered, 0.9689 vs 0.9471, and worst-of-the-pair when the world is reversed, 0.9312 vs 0.9448) is consistent with 'the arm carrying the world's own order wins by realizability, whichever order that is', and (a)/(c) are mirror images of one another by construction, so nothing here favours P>C>E>O specifically. What does not survive: (1) every number is a training-set accuracy (lines 160-163), so no generalisation claim exists; (2) the status word CAS_PRECEDENCE_VALUE_NOT_ESTABLISHED was not emitted by the program -- with (c) FAILED the script printed the line-251-253 'PREDICTION DID NOT HOLD AS REGISTERED / do NOT substitute a new hypothesis' branch, and the commit message substituted one anyway; (3) the order-specific effects +0.0219, -0.0136, -0.0061 are at the 5-seed noise level (seed sd 0.0301; author's own '~1 seed sd'), tested against fixed constants 0.02/0.03/0.05 with no paired analysis, and the same match-vs-mismatch quantity realised as >=0.0219 in (a) and 0.0136 in (c) straddles the 0.02 line; (4) 'order matters' is carried by the chain-vs-bag gap, which is a 480-vs-224-parameter, recurrent-vs-additive capacity asymmetry, not an order effect; (5) 3 of 24 orders tested. Plain reading: the specific CAS order P>C>E>O shows no intrinsic advantage in this harness, but the harness as committed cannot license that as a measured result either -- it is a training-fit readout with a prose-assigned status.

cas_only_reasoner/CJT_PREC_CLOSURE/p6_order_test.py lines 160-163:
    rng = np.random.default_rng(1000 + sd)

findings.title: World / answer-key check: no hidden channel to the label beyond test==train; the arms are architecturally identical to the generator, so 'order matters' is a property of the chosen world family
findings.evidence: Line 60 (world): s = np.tanh(E[:, t, :] @ A[j] + s @ B[j].T); line 105 (arm): h = np.tanh(E[:, order[j], :] @ p['W'][j] + h @ p['U'][j].T + p['b'][j]). Same recurrence, same H=8 (line 39), so the arm whose order equals true_order is an exact re-parameterisation of the teacher; non-matching arms are not. The true order (lines 181-184) is never passed to any arm: line 164-166 hands each arm only (order, Etr, ytr, Ete, yte), identical across arms. E is i.i.d. N(0,1) per slot (line 54) and y is a deterministic function of E, so there is no side channel. The three chain arms share identical init (line 165, seed 7000+sd; my check [6]: W identical); the bag's R differs because line 93 skips the U draws and shifts the RNG stream (minor asymmetry). Line 246-247 itself says 'ORDER IS A PROPERTY OF THE TASK'.
findings.effect_on_conclusion: No arm holds an answer key beyond the disclosed condition sweep. But the same builder chose a world family that is by definition an order-sensitive K-step tanh recurrence and an arm family that is that recurrence; 'order matters' for this family is true by construction and says nothing about any other task. Combined with the train==test defect, the experiment establishes neither 'order matters' nor 'CAS order has no value' as generalisation claims.

p6_lenses.world_generation_answer_key: The world's true order is a swept CONDITION (lines 181-184: CAS_ORDER, REVERSED, per-item random at line 73, and a bag world at line 86) and is never handed to an arm: run_condition (lines 164-166) gives every arm the same Etr/ytr/Ete/yte and only the arm's own fixed order. In condition (a) the CAS arm's order (0,1,2,3) equals the world's true order and in (c) the reversed arm's does -- this is the disclosed design, not a hidden key. E is i.i.d. N(0,1) per slot (line 54) and y = argmax(s @ C) is a deterministic function of E, so no content side channel exists (my single-slot OLS shows the last-processed slot is the most linearly readable: held-out 0.5519 for t=3 in (a), 0.5439 for t=0 in (c), but that is order structure, not a leak). The one true answer key is that the evaluation set IS the training set (lines 160-163; verified 20/20 identical). Secondary: arm recurrence (line 105) is architecturally identical to the generator recurrence (line 60), so the matching arm is an exact re-parameterisation of the teacher and 'order matters' holds for this world family by construction; and for the same seed, conditions (a), (c) and (b) share identical A, B, C and E (verified), differing only in composition order.
p6_lenses.registered_before_run_verifiable: No. The script's only commit is 1e58d7254d97c88effa609f7ad05ee2fca9b1aee (2026-09-02 21:29:49 -0700), and the results (0.9689, 0.9471, +0.0219, 0.9312, 0.9448, -0.0136, 0.7245, 0.7307, -0.0061, 0.0301) appear only in that same commit's message. The assertion 'written before running' exists in the docstring (lines 15, 17) and the printed banner (line 174) only; no prior commit, hash, or timestamped preregistration artifact exists. No run output was committed at all.
p6_lenses.held_out_is_held_out: NOT held out. Lines 160-162: `rng = np.random.default_rng(1000 + sd)` / `Etr, ytr = worldfn(rng, NTR)` / `Ete, yte = worldfn(np.random.default_rng(1000 + sd), NTE)  # same world, fresh draw`; line 163 `Ete, yte = Ete[:NTE], yte[:NTE]` is a no-op because line 40 sets NTR = NTE = 1500. Each worldfn draws A, B, C and then E (and, for the random world, the per-item permutations) from that single stream, so two fresh generators seeded with the same integer 1000+sd produce the same params, the same E and the same y. Verified by this audit with numpy (scratchpad check #1, exec of the committed blob's definitions only): np.array_equal(Etr, Ete) == True and np.array_equal(ytr, yte) == True for all 20 (condition, seed) pairs: (a), (c), (b), (NEG) x sd 0..4, shapes (1500, 4, 5). Consequently line 147-148 scores every arm on its own training data; every accuracy reported in the commit message is a training-fit number. The comment 'fresh draw' and the banner '1500 train / 1500 held out' (line 173) are false. Note the intended 'same world, fresh draw' cannot be produced by changing the seed with these function signatures, because a different seed also redraws A, B, C (a different world).
p6_lenses.arms_matched: Data: identical Etr/ytr/Ete/yte for all four arms per seed (lines 161-166). Optimiser: identical for all arms -- Adam-style with beta 0.9/0.999, eps 1e-8, LR = 0.05, STEPS = 700 full-batch (lines 40, 116, 139-146). Parameters (my count from init(), line 91-95): each chain arm W=160 U=256 b=32 R=32 total 480; BAG W=160 U=0 (line 93 zeros U, line 129 zero-grads it) b=32 R=32 total 224. Init: the three chain arms receive bit-identical initial W, U, b, R (line 165, default_rng(7000+sd)); the bag receives the same W but a different R because skipping the U draws shifts the RNG stream (verified: W identical True, R identical False) -- minor. Asymmetries that matter: (1) the BAG has 256 fewer parameters and no recurrence, so every chain-vs-bag margin (the POSITIVE control at line 204 and the commit's 'BAG loses by 0.13-0.15') is confounded with capacity, and the bag loses by MORE (0.1556/0.1558/0.1618) in world (b) where no order can be matched than in (a) 0.1508 or (c) 0.1236; (2) chain arms are architecturally identical to the world generator (line 105 vs line 60), so the order-matching arm is a teacher re-parameterisation; (3) only 3 of 24 fixed orders are arms; (4) all margins are training-fit, where the 480-parameter arms memorise 1500 points far above what an 84-number linear rule fits (0.7252 in (a)).
p6_lenses.verdict_on_specific_cas_order_value: NO VERDICT is licensed by this script. As committed, the script's own deterministic branch ends at lines 251-253 ('THE PREDICTION DID NOT HOLD AS REGISTERED') because d_c = -0.0136 fails the registered d_c < -0.02; the status CAS_PRECEDENCE_VALUE_NOT_ESTABLISHED (line 246) was never printed and lives only in the commit message. More fundamentally, every number is a training-fit accuracy (test set == training set, verified 20/20), the positive control is a capacity test rather than an order-matching test, and a genuine held-out check shows an 84-number linear rule at 0.7108/0.7092 (my measurement) that no arm is shown to beat out of sample (untracked repro: arm held-out max 0.6875 in (a), 0.6857 in (c), positive control FAIL). What survives as direction only: on training fit the CAS arm never beats the world-matching arm (d_c = -0.0136) and never beats the other fixed orders on random-order worlds (d_b = -0.0061), so nothing in the data points to a CAS-specific advantage -- but that is a null read from an instrument that cannot detect the property it was built to detect. Plain-English status: OPEN / NOT MEASURED. Neither 'P > C > E > O carries value' nor 'order matters but CAS order does not' is established by p6_order_test.py; the specific-CAS-order question remains untested until the held-out draw is repaired, a capacity-matched or linear mechanism-free baseline is registered, and a program (not prose) emits the status.
